steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Inflation is a sustained rise in the general price level, measured by the Consumer Price Index (CPI). The UK target is 2% CPI inflation.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Demand-pull inflation: too much demand chasing too few goods (e.g. booming economy). Cost-push inflation: rising production costs push prices up (e.g. higher oil prices, wage increases).

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Unemployment is when people able and willing to work cannot find jobs. Types: cyclical (recession), structural (skills mismatch), frictional (between jobs), seasonal (tourism, agriculture).

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Consequences of inflation: reduces purchasing power (especially for those on fixed incomes), savers lose value, uncertainty discourages investment, and UK exports become less competitive.

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: Explain the difference between demand-pull and cost-push inflation, giving a cause of each. | Describe three types of unemployment and explain what causes each. | Evaluate why there may be a trade-off between inflation and unemployment in the short run.

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Always specify the TYPE of inflation (demand-pull or cost-push) and the TYPE of unemployment. CPI measures a basket of goods — know that it's the official UK measure, targeting 2%. Consequences of inflation differ between groups: borrowers benefit (debt erodes), savers lose (value erodes).
